item.title: Customs to review complaints of 397 rejected recruitment applicants
item.description: By Efe Onodjae The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has announced plans to review complaints by applicants who were disqualified during its recent recruitment screening exercise despite appearing on the shortlist for training. The Service said the Comptroller-General of Customs, Bashir Adewale Adeniyi, ordered a case-by-case review after meeting with some of the aggrieved applicants. In a statement signed by the National Public Relations Officer of the NCS, Deputy Comptroller of Customs Abdullahi Maiwada, on Monday, the NCS said the review was aimed at ensuring that legitimate complaints were examined while maintaining the integrity of the recruitment process. It explained that appearing on the final shortlist did not automatically guarantee enlistment, as applicants were required to undergo several stages of verification, including credential checks, physical fitness assessments, medical examinations, age verification and drug screening. According to the Service, screening irregularities involving 397 applicants were identified in areas including substance use, physical fitness, medical records, age and submitted documentation. It added that some candidates were also disqualified over irregularities identified in their selection process. The NCS urged affected applicants who believe they were unfairly disqualified to submit their details and complaints to helpdesk@customs.gov.ng for review. It said applicants seeking reconsideration would be subjected to fresh screening, stressing that the review would not automatically guarantee admission into the training college. The Service further warned that applicants found to have engaged in criminal conduct, including certificate fraud and other offences, would be referred for appropriate legal action and prosecution. It urged the affected candidates and the general public to remain calm and use the designated channel to submit their complaints. item.title: ‘Close up your borders’ – Trump blames French unrest on immigration
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Monday again blamed immigration for protests and violence that have rocked France in recent days, urging Europe and French President Emmanuel Macron to tighten borders. “What’s happening in France has to do with immigration, not schools, not anything,” Trump told reporters in Washington, echoing his comments from the day before. “It’s immigration, and I told President Emmanuel Macron, close up your borders.” Weekend demonstrations over soaring prices were held in Paris and other cities, degenerating into some of the worst street violence France has seen in recent years. Trump recounted a conversation with Macron, telling him “a long time ago, you’re making a big mistake in France. You’re letting everybody from the world come in. The whole world was coming in. “Paris is going to be a Muslim city very soon,” the 80-year-old Republican added. “If Europe doesn’t close its borders and bring the criminals out, like the people that are protesting, Europe is finished.” Trump made combating illegal immigration a central pledge of his 2024 campaign, at times relying on false claims that played on racial fears. item.title: Maddison shines as Tottenham claim long-awaited first PL win of season
item.description: James Maddison made a sensational return to Tottenham’s starting line-up after 17 months away on Monday as Spurs beat Coventry 3-1 to claim their long-awaited first Premier League win of the season. The England midfielder has featured only fleetingly since May 2025, when he suffered the first of two serious knee injuries. But Maddison needed less than a quarter of an hour to put Spurs ahead at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium with a stunning first-time strike from outside the penalty area. Jack Rudoni levelled early in the second half but the home side were back in front just before the hour mark when Omar Marmoush lashed home his first goal for the club and substitute Ben Davies made the points safe late on. Roberto De Zerbi’s team came into the match bottom of the Premier League and with the unwanted record of being the only team in England’s top six divisions without a league win this season despite a huge summer spend. The Spurs boss had taken his squad to Marbella in southern Spain for some warm-weather training in a bid to kickstart their season. He named Maddison in his starting line-up while Sweden midfielder Dejan Kulusevski returned to the matchday squad for the first time in 17 months. Maddison ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee in August 2025, just three months after injuring the same knee. The 29-year-old wasted little time in making his mark, putting his side ahead in the 14th minute in spectacular style after fine work from Mohammed Kudus on the right. Maddison, lurking just outside the penalty area, received the ball from Kudus and sent it curling past Coventry goalkeeper Carl Rushworth and into the top corner, sparking wild scenes of delight among the home fans. Tottenham now had their tails up and threatened to overwhelm the visitors but Frank Lampard’s newly promoted Coventry, who had won their previous two games, re-established a foothold. Maddison went close to putting Spurs 2-0 after half an hour but his half-cross, half-shot curled narrowly wide. But they failed to stretch their lead and Coventry were level in the 49th minute, courtesy of a Rudoni strike from close range. Spurs lost the ball in the Coventry half and the visitors swept forward. Rudoni’s cross hit a teammate but the ball fell kindly for him and he drove home. Just nine minutes later Spurs were back in front when former Manchester City forward Marmoush held off Milan van Ewijk before unleashing an unstoppable shot. Kulusevski, who suffered a knee injury in May 2025, was introduced in the final minutes to a huge ovation from the home fans. Spurs veteran Davies made the three points safe deep into added time, poking home from the edge of the penalty area as Tottenham could at last relax. item.title: Florida issues arrest warrant for Cuba’s ex-leader Raul Castro
item.description: Florida’s top prosecutor announced an arrest warrant Monday for former Cuban president Raul Castro on state murder charges that echo a federal indictment unveiled earlier this year. Raul Castro, 95, is wanted on murder charges connected to the February 24, 1996 shooting down of two civilian aircraft from “Brothers to the Rescue,” an organization assisting Cubans fleeing to the US state by sea. “Raul Castro ordered the murder of four Floridians in cold blood, and Florida will never stop pursuing accountability for that communist conspiracy,” Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier said in a statement. Castro, brother of the late revolutionary leader and US nemesis Fidel Castro, was indicted on federal charges related to the incident in May. The move came as President Donald Trump’s right-wing administration steadily ramped up economic, political and legal pressure on the Cuban communist government. “We’re committed to pursuing every lawful, prosecutable avenue to bring accountability, including parallel federal and state prosecutions,” US Attorney Jason A. Reding Quinones said in a statement supporting Florida’s action. “We’re proud to stand with Florida in seeking justice for the four Americans murdered in the Brothers to the Rescue shootdown nearly 30 years ago,” the federal prosecutor said. In a statement on X, Cuba’s Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez condemned “the latest futile maneuver by anti-Cuban politicians in South Florida,” which he said was a “reflection of political rot and moral collapse.” Trump previously seized on a US indictment to justify military action in January that toppled Venezuela’s then-president Nicolas Maduro, a staunch ally of the Cuban authorities. Current Cuban President Miguel Diaz-Canel has said the US federal indictment against Castro has “no legal basis” and was an attempt “to justify the folly of a military aggression against Cuba.” AFP The post Florida issues arrest warrant for Cuba’s ex-leader Raul Castro appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Atiku’s ethnic, religious appeal won’t work in North – Iliyasu Kwankwaso
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Dr Musa Iliyasu Kwankwaso, has said former Vice President Atiku Abubakar cannot rely on ethnic and religious sentiments to win support in northern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Kwankwaso said political dynamics in the North had changed, arguing that voters were increasingly concerned about leadership performance, development and issues affecting their daily lives. He made the position known in a signed statement on Monday. He insisted that Atiku lacked the level of acceptance and political influence once enjoyed in the region by the late President Muhammadu Buhari. “Atiku is not Buhari. He does not possess the size, stature and acceptance of the late Nigerian President to pose a threat to Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” Kwankwaso said. The APC chieftain argued that Atiku could no longer assume that Hausa-Fulani voters would support him based mainly on ethnic or regional considerations. “The North has gone beyond primordial sentiment, and his penchant for relying on the ethno-religious card will certainly fail him,” he said. Kwankwaso also questioned Atiku’s record during his eight years as vice president. He argued that the former vice president had yet to present a convincing account of the development achievements from his time in office. He maintained that the 2027 election would be shaped by voters’ expectations of better leadership and improved living conditions rather than ethnic or religious loyalties. The APC chieftain further alleged that Atiku’s political associates were aware of his limited influence among Hausa-Fulani voters. Kwankwaso expressed confidence that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu would remain a strong contender in the North despite efforts by opposition groups to build a regional coalition against him. item.title: Drone Strikes Across Sudan Kill More Than 100 People
item.description: A wave of drone strikes targeting war-torn Sudan’s army-held capital Khartoum and two western areas controlled by paramilitary forces has killed more than 100 people since Sunday, according to residents, medical workers and paramilitary sources. The deadliest drone strike hit near a market on Sunday evening in Al-Dibab town in the southwestern state of West Kordofan, which is controlled by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) that have been at war with Sudan’s military since April 2023. Residents and medical workers said a drone struck a transport hub where villagers had gathered after a market day to find rides home, killing 80 people. Ahmed Abakar Wadi, a resident who helped bury victims, told AFP at least 50 bodies were recovered at the scene, including that of his brother. Another 47 wounded people were taken to the nearby town of Al-Mujlad where 30 later died from their injuries, according to a medical source. “The drone struck once, and then came back 10 minutes later and struck again,” Wadi told AFP. The RSF’s self-declared administration, known as Tasis, and the Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers accused the army of carrying out the attack. The military has not commented. The strike was one of the deadliest single attacks in Kordofan, an oil-rich region linking western and eastern Sudan where the army and the RSF have been battling for territory. item.title: APM to Tinubu: You’re paying fuel subsidy through back door
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Allied People’s Movement (APM) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of paying fuel subsidy through the back door, questioning the recent petrol price reduction despite the government’s declaration that subsidy was gone. The party also dismissed Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele’s warning that restoring subsidy could push the naira to ₦4,000 per dollar, describing the projection as unfounded and accusing the government’s economic policies of driving businesses into closure. APM National Secretary, Ayodele Adebayo, stated this in a response to Vanguard’s inquiries, faulting the administration’s handling of fuel prices and its claims about investors’ loss of confidence in opposition parties. “What are they doing now with the current reduction in petrol price for one month? Is it not returning subsidy through the back door?” Adebayo asked. He argued that the naira had previously exchanged at a stronger rate, rejecting the minister’s projection as an attempt to justify the government’s position on subsidy. Adebayo also challenged Oyedele’s claim that investors had written off opposition parties as unserious, alleging that harsh economic policies had forced several companies to shut down. “Where are even the investors that the Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, is talking about? Is it the recycled ones by the present administration?” he queried. The APM secretary said his party favoured an appropriate pricing framework for petroleum products to prevent further hardship, insisting that Nigerians should not be left with little money after paying for fuel. “We cannot subscribe to seeing Nigerians use all their entitlements and earnings to buy fuel due to harsh economic policies,” Adebayo said. item.title: Critic of Rwanda President Kagame beheaded in Uganda
item.description: A former Rwandan soldier living in Uganda, where he had become a vocal critic of his government back home, was found decapitated near Kampala, a police spokesperson said Monday. Rwandan authorities have been accused of assassinating opponents of President Paul Kagame, who has ruled the country with an iron fist since taking power in the aftermath of the 1994 genocide that claimed 800,000 lives, primarily among the Tutsi community. Robert Kabera, a former sergeant who fled Rwanda several years ago, was not outspoken during his time in the military but grew increasingly opposed to Kagame. His YouTube channel, “Major Robert TV”, which has 144,000 subscribers, included a song praising opposition figure Victoire Ingabire, a rare voice of dissent in Rwanda, who has been repeatedly imprisoned. Ugandan police said they were investigating the “murder of a male adult, (around 50), whose head was cut off, and up to now the head has not yet been recovered”, spokesperson Kituuma Rusoke told reporters on Monday, adding that the body had been identified by relatives as Robert Kabera. The body was found in Luwala, a village near Kampala, and the murder likely took place late on October 16 or early 17, he added. In Uganda, “Robert had no issues with anyone,” his brother, Victor Agaba, told AFP. “Our problem comes from home… The army created a criminal case against him. It was a witch hunt,” he said. Kabera was declared a fugitive after leaving Rwanda, and he was accused of corrupting a minor, which he denied. He is not the first opposition figure in exile to be assassinated. In 2021, a former lieutenant in the Rwandan army, Revocant Karemangingo, was shot dead in Mozambique, where he was suspected of secretly supporting an opposition force. Outspoken opponent Seif Bamporiki was gunned down in South Africa the same year, while a former Rwandan intelligence-chief-turned-critic, Patrick Karegeya, was strangled in his South African hotel room in 2014. Another exile, former general Faustin Kayumba Nyamwasa, who co-founded the Rwanda National Congress (RNC) opposition party with Karegeya, has survived several assassination attempts. item.title: All I want to hear in Rivers is Tinubu – Wike says in meeting with Fubara supporters
item.description: By Davies Iheamnachor Minister of the Federal Capital Territory and leader of the Rainbow Coalition, Nyesom Wike, has said that all he wants to hear in Rivers State is Bola Tinubu for a second term. Wike also declared that supporting President Bola Tinubu’s second-term bid is the strategic key to unlocking unprecedented political appointments, infrastructure development, and lasting national relevance for the oil-rich state. item.title: They thought I’d be sleepy – Tinubu thanks ADC for keeping him awake
item.description: By Bayo Wahab President Bola Tinubu has taken a swipe at the African Democratic Congress (ADC), thanking the opposition party for keeping him awake as he addressed supporters of the CityBoy Movement and the Relax Tinubu Is Fixing Nigeria (RTIFN) group. “Some people thought by now I would be tired and sleepy since I arrived here on time, thank you ADC,” Tinubu said during a ceremonial meeting with the support groups in Abuja on Monday. The remark comes as Tinubu prepares for the 2027 presidential election, in which former Vice President Atiku Abubakar is the ADC’s presidential candidate. The President said the grassroots mobilisation efforts of the support groups would allow him to rest easy, expressing confidence in their reach and organisational structure. According to him, the CityBoy Movement had introduced a new approach to political mobilisation by building a network beyond the gathering of crowds at political events. “The CityBoy Movement, to all of you, you have done something new in Nigeria politics. You did not just gather people; you built a structure, millions of real, verifiable members,” he said. Tinubu highlighted the group’s claimed nationwide presence, saying its structure extended from the state level to local governments, wards and polling units. “You have a presence in every state, every local government, every ward, down to the polling units,” he said. The President also praised the group’s engagement with young Nigerians through its call centre and community outreach initiative, CityBoy Care. “You drilled down; a call centre that speaks to young Nigerians every day and listens to whatever their community needs. CityBoy Care, meeting members where they live,” Tinubu said. He described the movement’s activities as evidence of organised grassroots engagement, rather than publicity-driven mobilisation. Tinubu said the group’s efforts in reaching communities and responding to their needs had strengthened his confidence in its political mobilisation ahead of the next election. With the movement working at the grassroots, the President said, he could return home and “sleep soundly”. item.title: National grid stabilised after ‘multiple trippings’ – NISO
item.description: The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) says it has put in place corrective measures to stabilise the national grid following multiple trippings on Monday. The management of NISO said this on its verified X handle in Abuja. It said: “NISO wishes to inform the public that at approximately 12:40 p. m. on Monday, the grid experienced multiple trippings on the 330 kilovolt (kV) transmission network.” The system operator said that following the incident, it immediately implemented appropriate corrective measures to stabilise the power system and restore normal operations. It said that restoration efforts had been successfully completed, and the grid has returned to normal operation. ”NISO wishes to clarify that the incident affected only a section of the grid, contrary to unverified reports and claims currently circulating in the media, ” it said. According to NISO, members of the public are. therefore, advised to disregard misleading information and rely on official communication channels for accurate and verified updates on the status of the grid. It said that NISO remains committed to maintaining grid stability, ensuring the reliable operation of the national electricity transmission system, and providing timely and accurate information to the public. (NAN) The post National grid stabilised after ‘multiple trippings’ – NISO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘You Cannot Ask Moses To Go Back To Egypt,’ Tinubu Insists No Fuel Subsidy Return
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has reiterated that there will be no return to the fuel subsidy regime, insisting that his administration took a bold and necessary step to reform the country’s economy. Tinubu spoke on Monday during a meeting with the City Boy Movement, a youth-driven political and advocacy group founded to champion his administration’s agenda. “I came, and I removed the subsidy on my first day. Nigeria would have gone bankrupt; there was nothing left to pay for subsidies,” he said. “I could listen to my political opponents promising a return to subsidy.” Drawing a religious analogy, the president added, “I remember my scripture studies, both in the Bible and the Holy Quran. When Moses (Musa) left Egypt, the Red Sea parted and gave way. You cannot ask Moses to go back to Egypt. With your energy and support, we will never go back to Egypt.” The former Lagos State governor commended the organisation for drumming up support for his administration and urged members to take his government’s achievements to the grassroots. “Those of you who are lucky to work with me have given me all the answers needed and the confidence required to see the coming election as a simple matter,” Tinubu stated. “You will go to your campuses, your markets, and your villages. Make sure every young person you know has a PVC and uses it. Tell them what we have done and tell them what we will do. Campaign with your ideas.” President Tinubu announced an end to fuel subsidy during his inauguration in May 2023. The policy shift sparked an immediate hike in petrol pump prices, rising from under ₦200 per litre to current rates hovering between ₦1,350 and ₦1,405 per litre across major filling stations. While the policy has drawn widespread criticism over the heightened cost of living, the president remains firm on his stance. The federal government maintains that the decision is essential to reset the national economy, reassuring citizens that the initial economic hardship will ease over time. item.title: 2027: Amupitan assures INEC workers of improved welfare, remuneration
item.description: The National Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan (SAN), has assured its staff members of improved welfare and remuneration ahead of the 2027 general elections. Amupitan gave the assurance while addressing INEC Staff in the South-East on preparedness for the 2027 General Elections in Enugu on Monday. The chairman came on a working visit to interact with traditional rulers and electoral stakeholders of the South-East. item.title: NAF airstrike kills ISWAP leaders in Lake Chad
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Precision strikes by the Nigerian Air Force (NAF), operating under Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), have neutralised scores of ISWAP terrorists in the Lake Chad region following the interdiction of an identified terrorist hideout on Monday. Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, Director of NAF Public Relations, said the operation underscores the NAF’s sustained commitment to degrading terrorist networks, disrupting their logistics and enhancing security across Nigeria’s North-East. According to him, “Preliminary post-strike assessments indicate that several prominent Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters were neutralised. “They include individuals identified as key figures within the group’s security structure and leadership Council, like Jindullah, reportedly the Chief Security Guard and confidant of Abu Saleem as well as Abul KissaI, a member of ISWAP Shura Council. “The strike also destroyed logistical assets, including boat engines and motorcycles, believed to support the group’s movement and operational activities. “The operation demonstrates the NAF’s intense effort to conduct intelligence-led precision strikes against terrorist enclaves concealed within difficult terrain. “By neutralising key operatives and destroying critical logistical resources, the strike delivers a significant setback to ISWAP’s operational capability, further constraining its ability to coordinate activities and threaten vulnerable communities. “Commenting on the success, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, reaffirmed the NAF’s resolve to sustain decisive air operations against terrorist networks in support of ongoing efforts to restore peace and stability across the country. “The Nigerian Air Force remains committed to working closely with sister Services and other security agencies to consolidate operational gains, protect vulnerable communities and advance efforts towards lasting peace and security in the North-East.” The post NAF airstrike kills ISWAP leaders in Lake Chad appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘I’m very proud of you’ — Tinubu showers praise on CityBoy Movement
item.description: By Bayo Wahab President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday praised the City Boy Movement for what he described as a new model of political organisation in Nigeria, telling its members he was “very proud” of them. The President spoke at the State House during a ceremonial meeting with the group and the Relax Tinubu is Fixing Nigeria (RTIFN) support group. Addressing members of the movement, Tinubu said the group had introduced something new to the country’s politics by going beyond mobilising crowds. “The CityBoy Movement, to all of you, you have done something new in Nigeria politics. You did not just gather people; you built a structure, millions of real, verifiable members,” the President said. He highlighted the group’s national spread, noting that it has “a presence in every state, every local government, every ward, down to the polling units.” The President also commended the movement’s engagement with young people, citing its call centre and its community outreach programme, CityBoy Care. “You drilled down; a call center that speaks to young Nigerians every day and listen to whatever their community needs. CityBoy Care, meeting members where they live,” he said. Tinubu described the group’s approach as organised and purposeful, rather than the product of mere publicity. “That is not noise. That is organisation. That is excellent thinking. That is the kind of seriousness this country needs from its young people, and I’m very proud of you. I must say so,” he said. The President also thanked members for defending his administration publicly, including at moments when doing so carried a political cost. “You were patient when patience was hard. You defended this administration in the market, on the campuses, at the motorparks and on social media even when it was not popular to do so,” Tinubu said. He added that their loyalty had not gone unnoticed. “I saw it, I noticed, and I will never forget it. I say thank you once again,” the President said. The City Boy Movement was founded by the President’s son, Seyi Tinubu, who is also its patron. item.title: Saudi postpones top investment conference to 2027 after Houthi attacks
item.description: A major Saudi investment conference has been postponed to next year, its chief executive officer said on Monday, as the kingdom comes under repeated attacks from Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis. The annual Future Investment Initiative (FII), often dubbed “Davos in the Desert”, was scheduled to take place from October 26-29. For nearly a decade, it has served as a showcase for Saudi Arabia’s efforts to attract global investors, business leaders and heads of state. The postponement deals a blow to the kingdom’s ambitions to draw foreign capital, diversify its oil-reliant economy and push its reform agenda. In a statement posted on X, FII Institute CEO Maha Al Saud said the gathering would instead take place in 2027, saying organisers wanted to ensure the anniversary edition delivered the “full scale” and “extraordinary quality” expected by participants. She said new dates would be announced soon, while current registrations and partnerships would remain valid. Three sources familiar with the matter had earlier told AFP the conference would be postponed. One source said organisers “won’t announce a new date soon” while another questioned who would be willing to “risk flying to Riyadh these days”. The decision comes after Riyadh’s international airport, a repeated target of Houthi attacks, suspended operations earlier this month after 13 people were killed in an October 10 strike, with no clear timeline for when air traffic could resume. It was the deadliest attack on the kingdom in more than a decade. Earlier this month, diplomatic sources said the kingdom was planning to move ahead with the conference, offering on-site and virtual attendance, as well as alternative air and land travel routes. But that plan appears to have been scrapped as Western travel warnings for the region have multiplied and the airport remains shut. “The executives I’ve spoken to are very, very, very hesitant to travel to Riyadh for this month’s conferences,” a consultant who advises Saudi firms told AFP. “Companies won’t put their employees in harm’s way for the sake of an investment conference,” they added.
